newsitem.title: USA: Rains delay harvesting of Minnesota corn, soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Rains delay harvesting of Minnesota corn, soybeans.

text.p: Rain late last week delayed harvesting of corn and soybeans in Minnesota, the state's agricultural statistics service said.

Corn was three percent harvested, as of Sunday, up from one percent a week earlier but behind the five-year average of five percent. It was 43 percent mature, up from 25 percent the previous week but behind the average 61 percent.

Soybeans were three percent harvested, also up from one percent a week earlier but behind the normal 12 percent. Eighty-three percent were shedding leaves, slightly ahead of the average pace of 79 percent.
Rains also slowed seeding of fall crops. Winter wheat, however, was still 99 percent seeded, up from 94 percent a week earlier and the normal 86 percent.
Rye seeding was also ahead of normal at 87 percent complete, versus a five-year average of 84 percent.
"Reporters forecasted that it would be the middle of next week before field work could resume," the report said.
Topsoil moisture was rated six percent surplus, 62 percent adequate, 23 percent short and nine percent very short.
